newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse bearish despite small-caps gains.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse bearish despite small-caps gains.

text.p: Second-tier listings from the Bucharest bourse occupied centre stage on Wednesday, but losses posted by seven of eight heavyweights dragged the market down, traders said.
"Both local and foreign investors showed some interest in small-caps, but the thin liquidity of the second section failed to keep the market from slipping," one said.
Traders said the market would keep a bearish phase in the next few days when selling pressure on first-tier listings is expected to grow.
Twenty-two of 40 stocks on the lower tier climbed, 11 fell and four stayed flat. Two companies had no trade and one was suspended.

Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation, went down by 2.36, 1.98 and 2.24 percent respectively from Tuesday due to falls in the average prices on the upper tier.
Selling pressure sent high-caps down with traders saying that buyers still believed prices were too high for a good placement. Local and small speculators moved to take some profits.

Azomures fertiliser maker closed 100 lei weaker at 3,500, while chemical plant Oltcim slipped 200 lei to 4,200. Some traders said Oltchim might slip further to a treshold of 4,000 lei, when a buying mood would set in.

Pharmaceutical plants Antibiotice and Terapia closed at 7,900 and 10,400 -- falls respectively of 250 and 1,200 lei and traders expected them to fall further. Arctic Gaesti refrigerator maker remained suspended.
Second-tier fittings maker Armatura was in high demand, closing 350 lei stronger at 6,000. Canning factory Amep also firmed 160 lei to end at 1,500.
